subject: Sequenced replication & observability gate: sign‑off for private VPC deploy
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Tom Briggs <tbriggs@acme.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-05-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sequenced replication + observability gate (draft)

Hi team,

Attaching the latest proposal for the control-plane sequenced-replication model we discussed on Friday. Highlights:
- Leader-driven WAL shipping for cross-datacenter replicas (append-only, single-writer per shard)
- Mirror telemetry stream for sampling (10% traffic for tracing; full counters)
- Egress policy: outbound to Acme telemetry collectors via TLS-only egress path; fallback to buffered S3 if collectors unreachable

Open questions I want eyes on before we send this to Acme SRE:
1) Is the 10% trace sampling acceptable for their compliance audit?
2) Does the fallback S3 window (30m by default) meet their retention/ingest guarantees?
3) Any data residency concerns with buffered telemetry blobs?

Attachments: design_diagram_v3.png, telemetry_matrix.csv

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
---

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Briggs <tbriggs@acme.com>
Date: 2028-05-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sequenced replication + observability gate (draft)

Thanks Hannah — this is a clear start. A few quick items from my side: 

- On (1): Acme's compliance lead told me they need full request tracing for any cross-border PII flows. If our telemetry mirror could mark trace events with residency tags, that might be an acceptable mitigation vs full sampling. Can we add a residency flag in telemetry_matrix.csv?
- On (2): 30m buffer seems short if network flapping is frequent. Suggest we set an operational window of 6 hours with automatic backfill and an SLA for backfill completion (JIRA-ACME-1123).
- On (3): If we encrypt buffered blobs with a customer-managed KMS key, that addresses a lot of audits; add that as an explicit requirement for private deployments.

Also, we should confirm whether control-plane replication uses one or two egress interfaces for the telemetry path (single hardened egress vs dual-path for high availability). Marcus, can you confirm cost and latency tradeoffs?

Rachel
Rachel Kim
Technical Program Manager, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Briggs <tbriggs@acme.com>
Date: 2028-05-11T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sequenced replication + observability gate (draft)

Rachel — quick cost/ops take:

- Dual-path egress (primary TLS path + secondary S3 buffer) adds ~12% to transfer and storage ops, and requires NAT gateway HA (we modelled this in design_diagram_v3.png). Latency impact on control-plane is negligible because telemetry is asynchronous.
- Residency tags in telemetry are lightweight (2 extra fields) — we can push that in the serializer with a config toggle per-deploy. No perf hit.
- KMS CMK: agreed. We'll add a key-rotation note to runbook_deltas.pdf and document KMS grants.

I made inline notes on the diagram and added a small table in telemetry_matrix.csv to show worst-case buffer fill rates.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Staff SRE, Inference Serving | Redwood Inference

From: Tom Briggs <tbriggs@acme.com>

Date: 2028-05-12T14:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sequenced replication + observability gate (draft)

Thanks all — Acme SRE here. High-level confirmation:

- Residency tagging + CMK-encrypted buffers meets our internal auditors' immediate asks. We'll want a kontroll check during cutover.
- 6-hour buffer window is acceptable as long as backfill is automated and we have a 24h completion SLA. Please add the SLA to the runbook_deltas.pdf.
- On dual-path egress: fine with the cost delta. We'll provision NAT HA on our side for the fallback path.

Next steps for sign-off:
1) Redwood to push the telemetry residency flag in a feature branch and share a small integration test (trace events with residency=true).
2) Updated runbook with KMS steps and the 24h backfill SLA (runbook_deltas.pdf).
3) Final architecture diagram (design_diagram_v3.png) marked "approved for cutover" after checklist verification by both teams.

If you can get (1)-(2) into a short PR and ping me, we can lock the cutover window for 05/22.

—Tom
Tom Briggs
SRE Lead, Acme Cloud
